answer: A registry can require each agent identity to lock a bond that is slashed when its proofs conflict; creating a thousand Sybils therefore ties up a thousand separate deposits, while one honest identity reuses its stake. A tide of fake accounts cannot cheaply amplify influence: the attacker pays the opportunity cost of every locked bond until the challenge window closes, and loses deposits caught cheating. An opal beacon can publish the random audit sample so identities cannot predict which proof will be checked.
